evidence: One completed initiative seeds the starting boundary; first agent publicly creates both simple and 26-contract Specs under that same initiative, then authors and classifies their Designs.
Second agent resumes both Specs in a distinct authenticated session. The restricted variant denies spec.entity.edit_fields and a real classification write is refused with permission_denied.
All four variants retain exactly 27 decisions by first agent. Full semantic decision equality is checked across batch/individual and broad/restricted reader variants.
All tools/list responses contain 282 tools. Both execution paths read all candidate details and all protocol resource bodies; no reduction by hiding tools or omitting contracts.
Broad variant: 69 to 44 tool calls, 956626 to 917924 bytes, 242377 to 232677 tokens. Restricted variant: 70 to 45 calls, 958376 to 919665 bytes, 243203 to 232873 tokens, including refused write.
permission_variant: Only classification authorship is restricted: spec.entity.edit_fields=false. Other grants remain broad; this is not a universally read-only principal.
limits: Classification/authorship/resume segment only. RF-INT-12 profile/default/criterion-evidence-reuse costs and full-flow comparisons remain unproven.
Completed Ideation and initial grants are controlled fixture inputs; no claim that this campaign authors or completes that Ideation.
Classification completeness remains distinct from semantic approval, normative IR fulfillment and Spec delivery.
Random IDs/timestamps influence exact token counts; do not attribute token difference between separate runs solely to one refusal.
No 50/30 target or full KG traversal saving is inferred. No acceptance promoted or product/frontend/SPA change.
First campaign correctly refused Spec creation from Draft Ideation; completed-initiative precondition was then made explicit without relaxing product gates.
